# Boss art prompts — Chaos Arena (generated by art/bosses/build.mjs — do not edit by hand)

Bosses 100+ (bosses-100-feature.md §7.1): the three trophy skins and the three boss badges.
Until a sheet is painted the game ships its procedural drawing (art/bosses/painters.mjs) at the target.

Paint: attach the finish references listed under a heading FIRST, the layout reference LAST, then paste ONLY the fenced
block.
Or `pnpm art:desk` → search the sprite name → Copy image, then prompt. Returns are sliced by
art/bosses/slice-return.mjs.

## Cinder — The Cinder Tyrant trophy skin  (single-cinder.png → images/models/cinder_256x256.webp)

Attach, in this order: `public/images/models/salamaner_256x256.webp`, `public/images/models/boulder_256x256.webp`, then
`art-sheets/bosses/single-cinder.png` LAST.

(If the return sits on a grey backing plate, re-paint with `art/skins/round/prompt-cinder-free.txt` and finish refs
only — art/skins/README.md.)

```text
WHAT COMES BACK IS ONE SPINNING-TOP SKIN, CENTRED, ON FLAT MAGENTA.
One square image, 1024 x 1024 pixels, holding exactly ONE top-down spinning-top skin in the middle, sitting exactly where the grey shape sits in the LAST attached image.
· 1 skin. Not 2, not 4 — and not a scene, a poster or a product shot.

WHAT THE ATTACHMENTS ARE — read this before anything else.
· The LAST attachment is the LAYOUT REFERENCE (one grey shape on magenta). Its flat grey shapes are NOTATION: they fix each skin's OUTLINE, SIZE and CENTRE, the small hexagonal badge in the middle and the ring around it. Take nothing else from it — not its grey, not its flat fills, not its thin lines. A result that comes back as the same grey shapes neatly shaded is a trace of the placeholder, and it is unusable.
· THE GREY IS NEVER PAINTED. No grey plate, backing, base, border, frame or shadow in the shape of the grey drawing may appear anywhere — not behind the skin, not around it, not peeking out between its parts. The skin's OWN painted parts (wings, points, frame, blocks) fill that outline; wherever the skin does not reach, the pixel is magenta. A skin sitting on a grey cut-out of the placeholder is the most common way this goes wrong.
· Every other attachment is a STYLE REFERENCE: a finished skin from the same game. Copy its FINISH — the ink, the shading, the highlights, the level of detail, the hexagonal-badge construction — and NEVER its subject. No skin may show leaves or a tree, a bird or feathers, or any other skin shown in them or anything else taken from them.

WHAT IT IS — skins for "Chaos Arena", a spinning-top battle game. A skin is the painted top face of one spinning top as the player sees it from directly above while it spins. Every skin is built the same way, from the centre out:
(1) a small HEXAGONAL BADGE in the exact centre, holding one simple icon;
(2) one or two concentric rings around it;
(3) the themed outer rim, which makes the outline.

THE SKIN — Cinder: a round iron brazier spinning top: a smooth closed rim of black cast iron with FOUR riveted grate bars crossing a bed of glowing coals, thin molten cracks between the coals (nothing sticks out of the circle).
Colours: black cast iron #221e27 to #3b3640 with ash-grey rim highlights, coal glow #ff6a1a with #ffd27a hot cores.
Hexagonal badge: a single flame inside a ring.

THE CLASS SILHOUETTE — a "Round Guard" top, and the outline IS the gameplay, so it must match the grey shape: a smooth, closed circle with nothing sticking out, the same thickness, the same reach.
ROUND GUARD: a perfectly smooth, closed CIRCLE. Nothing sticks out of it anywhere — no spikes, horns, ears, blades, tentacle tips or points break the round edge.

THE VIEW — straight down the spin axis, like a coin lying flat, seen from exactly above.
· Round and radial, centred on the badge — NOT an ellipse, NOT tilted. No three-quarter view, no side wall, no underside, no spike or stem underneath, no perspective, no foreshortening.
· No cast shadow, no ground, no table, no floor, no scenery.

STYLE — polished mobile-game art, exactly like the style references:
· A bold dark contour around every shape — at its heaviest about 2% of the skin's diameter, the weight of a brush pen, not a technical pen. Hold the picture at thumbnail size: if the outline has thinned to a hairline there, it is several times too thin.
· Rich, saturated colour with two or three cel-shading steps per shape and a soft light from the top-left; a crisp white highlight painted ON the surface of metal, enamel, horn, shell, glass and anything glossy (a shine band or dot — never a four-pointed sparkle star or twinkle symbol floating over it).
· Chunky, readable shapes that still read at 64 pixels across, with fine surface texture (fur strokes, wood grain, rivets, scales, stitching) painted inside them.
· AN OBJECT WITH NO FACE IS NOT AN EXCEPTION. A drum, an anvil or a compass is painted to exactly the same standard as an animal, with the same ink, the same light and the same shine.
· AVOID — this is exactly how attempts go wrong: flat vector clip-art; pale hairline outlines; photorealism or a plastic 3D render; a perspective or three-quarter view; text, letters, numbers or runes; a soft glow or bloom around the rim; anything see-through or half-transparent; drop shadows.

LAYOUT / SIZE — measured against the image, not judged by eye:
· Centred exactly in the middle of the image.
· It reaches exactly as far as the grey shape: about 760 px across, 74% of the image width — not bigger. There is at least 120 px of magenta between the skin and every edge of the image.
· Every blade, spine, point, tusk and lobe ends inside that circle; nothing pokes out past it.
· The bottom-right corner of the image stays empty magenta.

BACKGROUND — this matters more than the style.
Fill every pixel that is not a skin with solid, flat, pure magenta #FF00FF, edge to edge — treat it as a green screen.
· EXACTLY #FF00FF — red 255, green 0, blue 255. Not pink, not rose, not purple, not a soft or tinted version of it.
· NOT transparent (never a grey-and-white checkerboard), NOT white, NOT a gradient, NOT a texture.
· No card, panel, frame, plate or circle behind a skin: the magenta touches the skin's outline on every side, including the gaps between arms, spikes and points.
· No glow, halo, drop shadow or vignette on the magenta. Any glow stays INSIDE the skin's own outline.
· The skins contain no magenta and no hot pink anywhere.
· The rich palette is for the SKINS. The ground is not part of the painting and is not toned with it: it stays a vivid, eye-hurting #FF00FF.

BEFORE YOU CALL IT FINISHED, count and check:
· Exactly one skin, centred, with a smooth, closed circle with nothing sticking out.
· A small hexagonal badge in its exact centre with its icon.
· Seen from straight above: round and flat, not oval, not tilted.
· Every pixel that is not the skin is flat, vivid #FF00FF.
· No text, labels, numbers or watermarks.

OUTPUT: one image, 1024 x 1024 pixels, 1:1 square, PNG. If your tool has an aspect-ratio control, set it to 1:1. No labels, captions, numbers or watermarks.
```

LAYOUT / SIZE — measured against the image, not judged by eye:

· About 760 px tall (74% of the image), exactly as big as the grey hexagon. At least 120 px of magenta between the badge and every edge.
· Nothing — no flame, icicle, fur or crust — pokes out more than 20 px past the grey hexagon.
· The bottom-right corner of the image stays empty magenta.

BACKGROUND — this matters more than the style.
Fill every pixel that is not the badge with solid, flat, pure magenta #FF00FF, edge to edge — treat it as a green screen.
· EXACTLY #FF00FF — red 255, green 0, blue 255. Not pink, not purple, not a tinted version of it.
· NOT transparent (never a grey-and-white checkerboard), NOT white, NOT a gradient, NOT a texture.
· No card, plate or circle behind the badge; no glow, halo or shadow on the magenta. Any glow stays INSIDE the badge.
· The badge contains no magenta and no hot pink anywhere.

BEFORE YOU CALL IT FINISHED, count and check:
· Exactly one hexagonal badge, point up, centred.
· The emblem is a single flame (three tongues, orange with a yellow heart) inside a thick golden ring, big, in the middle of the field.
· Six studs or rivets on the frame's six corners.
· Every pixel that is not the badge is flat, vivid #FF00FF.
